# The Turkish number words a count claim can be written with.
#
# This file is DATA for TestTheCountsInTheProseAreTrue, not prose. Two documents
# in this repository are Turkish by decision (ADR 0012's ledger), and both of
# them state counts in words rather than digits, so the gate cannot read them
# without this vocabulary. It lives here rather than in count_claims_test.go
# because one of the words is on the language detector's own safe-word list:
# spelling it in a Go file would put a new line in the language ledger for text
# that is a lookup table, and the ledger may only shrink.
#
# Format: a value, a space, and the word, folded onto ASCII the way
# countFold folds a token it reads. One entry per line; "#" opens a comment.
# The units are 1 through 10 and the tens are 20 through 90; a compound is the
# two written as separate words, which is the form the READMEs use.
#
# countNumeralWords reads this file and refuses a short read, so deleting a line
# fails the gate instead of quietly narrowing what it can see.

# units
1 bir
2 iki
3 uc
4 dort
5 bes
6 alti
7 yedi
8 sekiz
9 dokuz

# tens
10 on
20 yirmi
30 otuz
40 kirk
50 elli
60 altmis
70 yetmis
80 seksen
90 doksan

# The scale words, marked with a value of 0: they are a HARD STOP rather than a
# multiplier, so a sentence above ninety-nine yields no claim instead of the
# number standing in front of the scale. They are here rather than in the Go
# source for the reason the units are.
0 yuz
0 bin
